sentences: `v_interp_p1/p2` weight the interpolation with the values their operand VGPRs hold at the two ops, not with the hardware's own pair.

Vonsek's image evidence on a synthetic triangle (#1224): zeroed sources render P0 = (0,0) on all 4,096 pixels, and copies of the pair read in swapped order render (v,u) — both follow the two VINTRP equations in the RDNA2 ISA guide; the centre interpolation the single-lane model used to emit is wrong for both.

When a write of the operand register reaches an interp site (earlier in its own basic block, or in any block a path runs through first — loops included; a write at the site itself, an interp whose destination is its own I/J register, happens after the operand is read), the attribute is read `PerVertexKHR` and both ops interpolate with the operand values loaded from `%vgpr`, which holds whatever the program computed: constants (snapped coordinates, 577 straight-line sites), copies and copy chains (575), arithmetic (8), multi-writer sequences (1,135).

The p1 loads its I and keeps it for the p2, which loads its J fresh — the program often sets J up between the two ops (574 sites) — so the final value uses the I of the p1 with the J of the p2; the p1's own full-sum value is dead because nothing may read the partial between the ops.

Pipodi's straight-line scan puts the upper bound at 213 PS (#1218 comment 7076614458; 2,290 v0/v1 sites plus one PS reading J through a copy, all branchy); the reaching-write analysis finds 207 with a write that can reach an interp, and 6 whose overwrites sit on paths that cannot (left pristine, `.spv` unchanged).
The other 11,888 PS keep the interpolated-input read and a byte-identical `.spv`.

Composes with the operand guards (row above, #1224): a pristine plain `v_mov` copy of the pair stays the guards' to model (centre interpolation, bit-identical `.spv`, including the corpus's one copy PS), an operand that is neither v0/v1 nor written stays the guards' role-naming refusal, and a computed site is exempt from `interp_pair_src` and modelled here — which relaxes exactly the guards' copy-based refusals whose operand a program write reaches: a twice-written register (`v_mov` then arithmetic — the load reads the value the later write left; value-proven by `test_copy_written_again_is_computed`), a copy of an already-overwritten v0/v1 (Vonsek's zero-before-copy row: hardware renders P0, which is exactly the loaded zeros), and a modified `v_mov_b32_dpp` source (any write of the operand is a `%vgpr` value; translation-only test).
A pristine copy in the wrong role still refuses (no computed value to model).

Over the corpus the relaxation is empty — every one of the 213 PS names v0/v1 (or the one qualified copy), so on main and on this branch alike the set translates 213/213 and passes `spirv-val` 213/213, and no shader changes class; the guards' refusals that relax are the synthetic ones the tests cover.

Refused (naming the pattern): a computed pair whose p1 partial is rewritten or read between the ops (its hardware value P10·I would be observable), one whose ops are not in one basic block (the captured I would not dominate the p2), a dangling op without its partner, any computed pair under `--bary-fallback` or `--f16-interp-fallback` (neither has PerVertexKHR inputs; the latter's decoded-half read would otherwise drop the computed weights), and a computed 32-bit read of a 16-bit-flagged interpolant — every one empty over the corpus.

Confirmed by `tests/semantic/test_interp_computed_ij.py` and `tests/semantic/test_interp_guards.py` (Vonsek's rows, the between-ops J, f16 pairs, the refusals, the relaxed classes) and the `ps_ij_computed` GPU test (RTX 5060 Ti: snapped quarter pair = 0.5, zeroed pair = P0 = 0, (i, j/2) halving the second weight with 0.0 max error over 4,096 pixels; the same fixture built on main is wrong on 4,096 of 4,096).
